title: a UTF-8 BOM prefixed onto a VAST 4.2 document is still classified and validated as VAST
specRef: IAB VAST 4.2 §2 (XML document conventions permit a byte-order mark before the prolog); packages/core/vast-shape.js documents skipping "a byte-order mark, whitespace, comments, processing instructions and a DOCTYPE" at offset 0 before matching the <VAST> root, specifically because plenty of partner systems emit one — this case proves bid.adm (which reaches no other BOM-stripping code path in the codebase) still classifies correctly.

preview.capabilityGap: The current VAST preview is inert XML; video/audio playback and Wrapper resolution are not implemented.

specNotes: The VAST document body is byte-for-byte the base pair's own adm; only a leading U+FEFF is added, so every other assertion mirrors video-x-web-42-inline-linear.json exactly.

ECMAScript String.prototype.trim() also strips U+FEFF as WhiteSpace, so the browser-side classifier (public/modules/inspector/creative-classify.js, which trims before calling the core isVastShape) agrees with the server-side scanner independently of the prolog-walker fix in vast-shape.js.
